title: Function-resolution verifier: precision & param-schema enforcement harness
creator: Marcus O'Neill
description: Build an automated evaluation harness that continuously validates function/tool selection precision and argument-schema correctness after config or model changes. The harness will run on every model/config canary and on daily scheduled jobs. Goals: detect regressions in top-1 selection accuracy, surface increases in invalid-arg generation, and correlate failures to config diffs (routing rules, selector weights) and model versions. This ticket covers design, data collection pipeline, a lightweight runner that executes synthetic and sampled real traffic prompts, and dashboards/alerts integrated into the Console and SRE channels.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI job that runs against a candidate model/config produces a digestible report with selection-accuracy, arg-schema-pass-rate, and examples of mismatched selections; 2) A Grafana dashboard with historical baselines and anomaly alert (>=5% drop in top-1 accuracy or >=3x increase in invalid args) wired to #sre-tooling; 3) Canary gating rule defined (block rollout if arg-schema-pass-rate < 97% on canary); 4) Documentation page and runbook merged at Confluence and linked from Console 'Regressions' view; 5) Unit tests and a small end-to-end runner in infra-evals repo with reproducible seed and synthetic dataset.
design_decisions: Use hybrid dataset: 50% synthetic adversarial prompts, 50% sampled production prompts (anonymized) to catch both edge-case and real-world regressions.
Compare candidate model+config against a stable baseline model variant to compute deltas; store per-route and per-customer breakdowns.
Argument validation uses JSON Schema for structured args plus custom heuristics (type coercion detection, missing required fields, improbable enum values).
Run harness in two modes: fast CI (1000 examples, <15m) for pre-merge, and nightly full run (50k examples) for historical baselining.
Alert thresholds conservative by default; on first rollout use alerts as paging-disabled notifications to SRE/PM for triage rather than blocking automatically.
Store results in time-series DB and object storage for diffs; keep raw anonymized traces for 30 days for debugging, derived metrics retained for 13 months.
Avoid heavy instrumentation on hot paths: use sampling hooks and shadowing for production traffic to collect ground-truth samples without impacting latency.
Privacy: redact PII from sampled prompts using the redaction pipeline before storing any example prompts for engineer review.
progress_updates: 2025-10-30: Spike complete. Implemented prototype runner that executes tool-selection calls against baseline and candidate models; initial metric schema defined.
2025-11-03: Telemetry schema proposed in PR #3891; landed basic metrics (top1_choice, top3_includes_groundtruth, arg_schema_ok). Review feedback requests clearer enum handling.
2025-11-06: Data retention plan reviewed with Security — agreed on 30-day raw trace retention with enforced redaction; Confluence doc updated (link below).
2025-11-09: Nightly full-run pipeline wired into infra-evals cluster; observed a transient +1.9% invalid-arg spike for model-beta-2025-11 on 2025-11-08 (root cause under investigation).
2025-11-12: Submitted PR for canary gating rules and dashboards (github.com/redwood-inference/infra-evals/pull/412). Moving to In Review for PM and SRE sign-off.
blockers: Need sample-consent confirmation for storing anonymized customer prompts from Privacy team (blocking full nightly run for prod-sampled data).
Arg-schema canonicalizer needs finalization: difference between 'coerce numeric strings' and 'strict type check' affects pass-rate dramatically; PM decision pending.
tradeoffs: Strict schema enforcement reduces false accepts but increases false positives for downstream callers that rely on permissive coercion. We propose a per-route policy: strict for high-trust internal tools, permissive-with-warnings for third-party connectors. This increases complexity in evaluation but aligns with customer expectations.
qa_plan:
- CI quick-run (1000 examples) must pass and produce <15m runtime.
- Nightly run validates historical baseline stability; if anomaly detected a secondary focused run (10k examples) executes to confirm.
- Manual review of top 20 failing examples per alert.
- Integration test that injects known malformed args to verify detector correctness (expected 100% detection).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: CI quick-run enabled on all PRs affecting tool-routing/eval code (non-blocking). Phase 2: Nightly full-run with sampled prompts enabled for non-prod datasets. Phase 3: Canary gating turned on for internal teams (block on arg-schema-pass-rate < 97%). Phase 4: Global gating after two successful canaries and PM/SRE sign-off.

notes: PM (Aisha Kapoor) requested an additional metric: 'semantic-arg-fitness' which is an ML model that scores plausibility of free-text args; added as low-priority follow-up. SRE asked that initial alerts only create tickets in the 'tooling' queue and not page during business hours until sensitivity tuning is complete.
example_failures: Model-candidate selected 'billing_query' tool for prompt about API latency (expected 'observability_query'); arg payload missing 'time_window' required field.
Candidate returned numeric id as string for 'user_id' causing downstream schema validation failure when strict typing enforced.
Selector drift: for route /chat/assistant, top1 selection delta -12% for 'payment_tool' after routing weight change in config-2025-11-02.
